bug_semantics: Apache Airflow's Backfill API authorization dependency (`requires_access_backfill` in api_fastapi/core_api/security.py) parsed the `backfill_id` path segment with plain `int()` and swallowed the ValueError as None, while the route handlers declared `backfill_id: NonNegativeInt`, which pydantic's lax mode validates differently: "1.0"/"1.00" coerce to 1 under pydantic but `int()` rejects them. FastAPI resolves dependencies before endpoint validation, so for those spellings the dependency left dag_id unset (falling back to the request body's dag_id, which the caller controls) while the handler served the request against backfill 1. An authenticated user holding edit permission on any single Dag could read, pause and cancel backfills of any other Dag — sequential ids make targeting trivial (CWE-436 Interpretation Conflict).
flaw_origin: Commit 5cfb58c7de36550dd34370ca261dc936d528a938 ("Fix backfill permissions (#62856)", 2026-03-04, author Pierre Jeambrun <pierrejbrun@gmail.com>, committer GitHub) wrote the divergent parser: it replaced `if backfill_id is not None and isinstance(backfill_id, int):` with `backfill_id_raw = ...; try: backfill_id = int(backfill_id_raw) ... except ValueError: backfill_id = None` — while the route handlers already declared `backfill_id: NonNegativeInt` (present in backfills.py at 5cfb58c7^, lines 101/125/152/178). From this commit the dependency's parser and the handlers' parser disagree on "1.0"-style ids, creating the interpretation conflict. Parent 45df4e5aea had a strictly narrower (fail-closed-ish) isinstance-int check; the parser divergence was born in 5cfb58c7.
